1. **PreMailer.Net/PreMailer.Net/PreMailer.cs:518 (`GetMarkupFormatterForDocType`)** — Making this method return `EmailHtmlMarkupFormatter.Instance` instead of `HtmlMarkupFormatter.Instance` silently changes the default output of `MoveCssInline` even when `preserveEntities` is left at its documented default of `false`. Since this method is only reached on the `preserveEntities == false` branch in `MoveCssInline`, entities like `©` will now *always* be preserved instead of converted to Unicode characters, contradicting the README's documented behavior of the `preserveEntities` parameter. Fix: keep entity-preservation strictly behind the `preserveEntities` flag — either make `EmailHtmlMarkupFormatter` only own the empty-tag fix and leave `GetMarkupFormatterForDocType()` returning `HtmlMarkupFormatter.Instance`, or have `EmailHtmlMarkupFormatter` take an `encodeEntities`/`preserveEntities` constructor flag so the two behaviors can be composed/toggled independently. 2. **PreMailer.Net/PreMailer.Net/Html/EmailHtmlMarkupFormatter.cs — `CloseTag`** — The override ignores the `selfClosing` parameter entirely and unconditionally emits ``. Void/self-closing elements (`
`, ``, `
`, ``, ``, ``, etc.) will now be serialized with a closing tag (e.g. ``), which is invalid HTML and can break rendering in the very email clients this library targets — an arguably worse regression than issue #171 itself. Fix: only force a closing tag for elements that are empty-but-not-void (mirror AngleSharp's own void-element check, e.g. via `element.Flags`/`HtmlElement` void-tag list) and preserve the base behavior (no closing tag / self-close) for actual void elements. 3. **PreMailer.Net/PreMailer.Net/Html/EmailHtmlMarkupFormatter.cs — `Text` entity replacement** — Reimplements entity preservation from scratch with a hardcoded 11-entry dictionary, duplicating and diverging from the existing `PreserveEntitiesHtmlMarkupFormatter` (which presumably covers a much larger/complete entity set) that's still kept around and used elsewhere (`preserveEntities` branch in `PreMailer.cs`). This leaves two inconsistent, independently-maintained definitions of "preserve entities," and silently drops support for any entity not in this short list (e.g. ` `, `…`, `—`, accented letters, quotes). Fix: have `EmailHtmlMarkupFormatter` delegate to/reuse `PreserveEntitiesHtmlMarkupFormatter`'s existing entity table (e.g. compose or inherit) instead of hand-rolling a subset. 4. **PreMailer.Net/PreMailer.Net.Tests/EmailHtmlMarkupFormatterTests.cs and PreMailerTests.cs** — No test exercises void/self-closing elements (``, `
`, `
`, ``) through the new formatter, which is exactly the case broken by issue #2. Fix: add a test asserting `` / `
` round-trip without gaining closing tags. 5. **PreMailer.Net/PreMailer.Net/Html/EmailHtmlMarkupFormatter.cs** — New public class has no XML doc comments, inconsistent with the documentation convention used throughout `PreMailer.cs` (every public method has a ``). Fix: add doc comments describing the class's dual purpose (empty-tag preservation + entity preservation) and why it's now the default formatter.
